name: biz.agentconcierge/agent-concierge
title: AgentValCon — Agent Value Gateway
description: Find AI agents for a task; run workflows built from agents we tested, in one call.

tools.name: hello
tools.description: Get a visitor token so later calls remember you (optional). Greets you and asks what you need. Use when you want this service to remember you across calls. Example arguments: {"name": "travel-planner-agent"}

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: chat
tools.description: Find an agent by describing your task in plain English and narrowing it over several turns ('only free ones', 'details 1', 'more', 'what's new', 'stop'). Keeps the conversation for your visitor token; replies are in English. Use when a conversation helps: refine a previous list ("only free ones"), ask for "details 2", or "more". Example arguments: {"message": "find a weather forecast API"}

message.description: Plain-English request or follow-up, at most 2000 characters.

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Compare up to three catalog agents for a task by name, grade and last successful check. Stateless and read-only; no conversation is saved. Searches A2A first, then MCP; x402 requires an explicit choice. price_status is free, paid or paid_or_unknown (price_usdc null). Returns the same ranked list as find_agents; use find_agents when you are ready to connect. Use when you want to browse and compare candidates for one task before choosing. Example arguments: {"task": "translate a document to Spanish"} Ads: at most one offer labelled "Sponsored" may follow the results in a separate `sponsored` field; it never changes the results.

task.description: The specific capability needed (e.g. 'weather forecast', 'stock price', 'web search')

kind.description: Explicit recommendation protocol filter; Any searches A2A then MCP, excluding x402. Defaults to A2A first, then MCP; x402 requires an explicit choice.

category.description: Compatibility field; task relevance is derived from the task text.

auth.description: Compatibility field; authentication preference does not affect ranking.

k.description: Compatibility field; at most three results is returned.

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: find_agents
tools.description: Get up to three recently verified agents for your task, with what you need to call each one (endpoint, verification evidence, calling details). Stateless and read-only; no conversation is saved. price_status is free, paid (price_usdc per call in micro-USDC) or paid_or_unknown (the provider states a price or none is known; price_usdc is null). A listing our gateway can run has connection_available (same as gateway_ready) and run_here: only when ready is true, pass its arguments to this server's call tool; otherwise ask for required_arguments before calling; mcp_config is a settings entry for an MCP host. Each result shows when the agent was last checked; before a later call, run check_agent on its endpoint, and if a call fails, call report with ok false for alternatives. Use when you want to connect to one of them now or run it here with call. Example arguments: {"task": "extract text from a PDF", "kind": "mcp"} Ads: at most one offer labelled "Sponsored" may follow the results in a separate `sponsored` field; it never changes the results.

kind.description: Explicit recommendation protocol filter; Any searches A2A then MCP, excluding x402. Defaults to A2A first, then MCP; x402 requires an explicit choice.

category.description: Compatibility field; task relevance is derived from the task text.

auth.description: Compatibility field; authentication preference does not affect ranking.

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: check_agent
tools.description: See an agent's recorded status, success rate and latency before you call it, with its grade, evidence sources and up to three alternatives (read-only, for an endpoint or agent-card URL). The URL is only looked up, never called. Use it before each call, also for agents we recommended earlier: status changes between checks. Use before each call to an agent, including one we recommended earlier, or when you already have an agent URL. Example arguments: {"url": "https://agent.example.org/.well-known/agent-card.json"}

url.description: The agent's endpoint or agent-card URL (public http or https).

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Re-check the evidence for the last task you saved with chat, without changing it. Use chat to save a task first (valid visitor token required). Use when you saved a task through chat earlier and want its evidence re-checked. Example arguments: {"visitor_token": "vt_..."}

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: call
tools.description: Run a read-only tool of a recommended agent through our gateway and get its answer in this session, after checking its current schema. Only tools classified read-only are relayed; destructive tools and tools that need the provider's own credentials are refused. A paid listing runs only with a payment proof you supply. Do not retry an uncertain outcome automatically. Use when you have chosen a listing and want this gateway to run one of its admitted tools. Example arguments: {"resource_id": 133020, "tool": "get_country_profile", "arguments": {"country_code": "US"}}

resource_id.description: The resource_id of the agent, MCP server, or API to call

tool.description: The specific tool name to execute

arguments.description: Key-value arguments to pass to the tool

task.description: The task query (optional; used to find immediate alternatives if execution fails)

account_id.description: Optional credit account ID for paid tools (defaults to your visitor ID)

payment.description: Optional payment details (tx_hash, signature, headers) for paid endpoints

idempotency_key.description: Stable caller key for supported ticketed delivery while its execution record is retained. Reuse with identical input; uncertain execution stays paused for review.

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: report
tools.description: Tell us whether a call worked; on a failure, get up to three currently verified alternatives and eligible published workflows (no retry is executed). Retain the selected protocol and reject known shared failure domains. Use after a call to record the outcome and, on failure, get verified alternatives. Example arguments: {"resource_id": 133020, "ok": false, "error_type": "timeout"}

resource_id.description: The resource_id of the agent/tool that was executed

ok.description: Whether the tool call succeeded (true) or failed (false)

error.description: Optional error message or reason on failure

error_type.description: Optional structured failure category. This report never authorizes a retry.

protocol.description: Optional explicit recovery scope; otherwise retain the prior selection.

task.description: The task query (optional; defaults to your last searched task)

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: credit
tools.description: Read your virtual credit balance (visitor token required). Top-ups and subscriptions are being prepared; this tool only reads the current balance. Use when you need your own credit balance before a paid call. Example arguments: {"action": "balance", "visitor_token": "vt_..."}

action.description: Action: balance to check your credits.

account_id.description: Your own visitor account ID (defaults to the authenticated visitor ID)

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: adapt_rest
tools.description: Turn a public OpenAPI document into tools you can call, or call one of its endpoints (action list_tools only reads the document; action call sends the request). A call sends the HTTP method the document declares, including POST, PUT or DELETE, to that public API without credentials, so it can change data there. Use when the API you need has an OpenAPI document but no MCP server. Example arguments: {"spec_url": "https://api.example.org/openapi.json", "action": "list_tools"}

spec_url.description: URL of the OpenAPI/Swagger JSON specification.

action.description: Action: 'list_tools' to discover executable tools, 'call' to invoke an endpoint.

tool.description: Tool name to execute when action='call'.

base_url.description: Optional override for API base URL.

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: search_workflows
tools.description: Find up to three ready-made multi-agent workflows (necklaces) for a purpose, by capability or common aliases. Discovery does not execute it. Use when a multi-step published workflow may already do your task. Example arguments: {"task": "country population indicators"}

task.description: The outcome you need, in plain language.

protocol.description: Optional explicit constraint on workflow node protocols.

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: workflow_details
tools.description: See a published workflow's steps and whether it is ready to run. Review inputs and use the existing authorized workflow run API to execute. Use after search_workflows to inspect one workflow's steps and readiness. Example arguments: {"template_id": 12}

template_id.description: The workflow id returned by search_workflows.

visitor_token.description: Your visitor token (vt_…) so I remember you. Omit on first contact.

tools.name: verify_agent
tools.description: Read-only check of one agent from our latest tests: result per role, score items out of 100, how accuracy was checked, whether it is a verified pearl, test time, response fingerprint, verified alternatives for the same role and, if one is offered, a necklace for the job. Give agent_id or url.

tools.name: best_for_role
tools.description: Read-only: the verified pearls (agents that passed our tests for this role) and the necklaces that run this job, if any is offered, from our latest tests. Roles look like weather.forecast.v1. Ads: at most one offer labelled "Sponsored" may follow the results in a separate `sponsored` field; it never changes the results.

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.description: Run one published workflow after reviewing it with workflow_details. Pass the definition_hash you reviewed; a changed workflow is refused. Ask for a task (params.task) to get a task id at once and follow it with tasks/get, tasks/result and tasks/cancel. Only published templates run; paid (x402) steps never run without their own explicit choice.

definition_hash.description: definition_hash returned by workflow_details for the version you reviewed.

input.description: Declared product input fields, when the workflow has them.

tools.name: necklace_airport_arrival_weather_brief
tools.description: Necklace (a workflow of tested agents: 2 verified pearls and 1 agent under verification): Check the destination airport, its current local time, and the ground-level daily forecast in one response. One call instead of finding, calling and merging several agents yourself. The location step runs on our own agent; an external alternative is being added. Scope: Ground-level destination weather for passenger planning. Forecasts can change. Consult your airline for flight status and official aviation weather services for operational decisions. Example arguments: {"code":"SFO"}. Free to run for now. If that changes, we will say so on its page first. Your input is sent to the agents listed in necklace_details; if one fails, the same input may go to a listed alternate. No credentials or payments are sent. Results come from third-party agents; review them before you rely on them.

detail.description: full (default) or brief: the same facts, values and links in fewer tokens.

tools.name: necklace_website_trust_brief
tools.description: Necklace (a workflow of tested agents: 3 verified pearls and 1 agent under verification): A trust brief on one domain: when it was registered, its SPF and DMARC mail records, its TLS certificate, and (optional) whether AI crawlers may read it. What each step uses (as of 2026-11-18, version 2): registration date and registrar come from RDAP (a verified third-party agent); mail authentication reads the domain's published SPF and DMARC records from DNS (a verified third-party agent); the TLS step reads the certificate the site presents (our own agent); the AI crawler check is optional. Which fallback each step has is listed under the agents below. DKIM is not checked: a DKIM record can only be looked up with the sender's selector, which a domain does not publish. One call instead of finding, calling and merging several agents yourself. The tls step runs on our own agent; an external alternative is being added. Example arguments: {"domain":"python.org"}. Free to run for now. If that changes, we will say so on its page first. Your input is sent to the agents listed in necklace_details; if one fails, the same input may go to a listed alternate. No credentials or payments are sent. Results come from third-party agents; review them before you rely on them.
